title: QED Astoria
venue_description:
QED Astoria

QED is an independent arts space in the heart of Astoria and the only woman-owned and operated venue of its kind in Queens. It runs a packed weekly calendar spanning comedy, storytelling, poetry, music and community events.

Atmosphere and Setting

QED has the feel of a small black-box theater rather than a bar, with rows of seating facing a stage — a format built for listening and paying attention to performers rather than background entertainment.

The Queens Poet Open Mic

On the first Saturday of the month from 3:30 PM to 5:00 PM, QED runs The Queens Poet, an open mic dedicated to poetry, singer-songwriters and spoken word, explicitly excluding stand-up comedy. Sign-up happens in person starting at 3:00 PM, with names drawn from a bucket for a three to five minute set. Musicians may use phone-connected backing tracks with the host's advance notice, and a five dollar minimum purchase is requested.

Other Programming

QED also runs a nightly general open mic series mixing comedians, poets and musicians, along with a wide range of comedy shows, storytelling nights and arts programming throughout the week, making it one of the busiest independent stages in the borough.

Good to Know

QED Astoria is located at 27-16 23rd Avenue in Astoria, a short walk from the N/W Astoria-Ditmars Blvd subway station.

title: Shillelagh Tavern
venue_description:
Shillelagh Tavern

Shillelagh Tavern is a traditional Irish sports pub in Astoria, a neighborhood gathering spot for sports viewing, drinks and live music several nights a week.

Atmosphere and Setting

The tavern keeps a classic pub feel — wood paneling, a long bar and a crowd that treats the place as a genuine local, with live music woven into its regular weekly rhythm rather than treated as a special event.

The Open Mic

Every Wednesday at 8:00 PM, the Astoria Music Collective runs a weekly open mic at the tavern, inviting local musicians to perform original songs and covers across all genres in a casual, welcoming setting.

Other Programming

The tavern's live-music calendar includes additional nights run by community groups, reinforcing its role as one of Astoria's more consistent grassroots music venues.

Good to Know

Shillelagh Tavern is located at 47-22 30th Avenue in Astoria.

title: The Local Bar
venue_description:
The Local Bar

The Local Bar is a neighborhood bar in Astoria that has grown into a genuine hub for local live music, hosting multiple recurring music nights throughout the month.

Atmosphere and Setting

The bar has an easygoing, community feel, drawing a loyal crowd of neighborhood regulars alongside performers who return week after week.

Saturday Songwriters Open Mic

Every Saturday, sign-up begins at 3:00 PM with the show starting at 4:00 PM. Hosted by the Astoria Music Collective, the open mic welcomes singer-songwriters playing original material and covers, and performers who sign up receive a free drink.

Other Programming

The Local Bar also runs additional live-music nights and community events throughout the month, including occasional open-jam-style gatherings, further cementing its role as a gathering spot for Astoria musicians.

Good to Know

The Local Bar is located at 41-04 31st Avenue in Astoria.

title: Bar Freda
venue_description:
Bar Freda

Bar Freda is a two-floor Ridgewood venue billed as an NYC rock venue downstairs with a lounge upstairs, operating as an LGBTQ+ safe space with live music booked most nights of the week.

Atmosphere and Setting

The downstairs room has the feel of a proper rock club — stage, PA and a crowd that comes specifically for the music — while the upstairs lounge offers a quieter space to unwind between sets.

The Underground Open Mic

Every Monday from 7:30 PM to 11:30 PM, with sign-up starting at 8:00 PM, Bar Freda hosts The Underground, a free open mic for music and spoken-word performers, hosted by Sunbeam Colleen, I'm Not Holden Caufield, and Road to Ruin.

Other Programming

Bar Freda advertises live music every night of the week, making it one of Ridgewood's most consistently active venues for local and touring rock acts beyond its Monday open mic.

Good to Know

Bar Freda is located at 801 Seneca Avenue in Ridgewood.

title: Terraza 7
venue_description:
Terraza 7

Terraza 7 is an intimate live-music venue in Elmhurst that has specialized in Latin, jazz, Caribbean and world music for more than two decades, seating around seventy guests in a warm, listening-room atmosphere.

Atmosphere and Setting

The room is small and personal, built around close-up listening rather than a bar-first crowd, and it has become a genuine community anchor for Queens' jazz and Latin music scenes.

Weekly Jazz Jam Session

Every Sunday from 8:30 PM to 11:55 PM, bassist John Benitez hosts what the venue calls the only weekly jazz jam session in Queens, blending Latin jazz, Brazilian music and straight-ahead jazz standards. All musicians are welcome to sit in, with a five dollar cover for mezzanine access.

Other Programming

Terraza 7 also partners with Queens College and community arts organizations on periodic jazz jam series for emerging musicians, alongside a full calendar of ticketed world-music and jazz shows throughout the year.

Good to Know

Terraza 7 is located at 40-19 Gleane Street in Elmhurst. The venue has weathered a lease dispute in recent years, so confirming current hours before a visit is a good idea.

title: Flushing Town Hall
venue_description:
Flushing Town Hall

Flushing Town Hall is a nonprofit performing arts center housed in a historic Flushing building, running a full calendar of theater, gallery exhibitions, education programs and live music for the Queens community.

Atmosphere and Setting

As a cultural institution rather than a bar or club, Flushing Town Hall offers a more formal, theater-style setting for its music programming, with a Steinway baby grand piano and a proper stage.

Monthly Jazz Jam

Held once a month year-round on a date that varies, the Monthly Jazz Jam is led by saxophonist Carol Sudhalter alongside Joe Vincent Tranchina, Scott Neumann and Eric Lemon. It welcomes professional jazz musicians, graduate music students, educators and serious hobbyists on all instruments and voice, with a full piano and drum kit provided. Non-musicians are welcome to attend as audience members.

Other Programming

Flushing Town Hall runs a wide range of concerts, exhibitions and educational programs throughout the year, occasionally including jazz-poetry open mic variants of the jam session.

Good to Know

Flushing Town Hall is located at 137-35 Northern Boulevard in Flushing. Because the jam's exact date shifts month to month, check the venue's calendar before visiting.

title: Grey Studios LIC
venue_description:
Grey Studios LIC

Grey Studios LIC is a recording and live-room studio space in Long Island City, used to host a recurring community open mic in partnership with the literary and arts organization Keepsake House.

Atmosphere and Setting

The studio setting gives the open mic a more intimate, community-oriented feel than a typical bar, with an emphasis on original work and a welcoming space for underrepresented artists.

Queens Open Mic

Held monthly on the first Sunday from 3:30 PM to 6:00 PM (doors at 3:00 PM), the open mic mixes music, storytelling and spoken word in an all-genre format, with BIPOC and LGBTQ+ artists performing original work especially encouraged. Performers get roughly two songs or ten minutes each, and the host rotates monthly. Online pre-registration is encouraged via Keepsake House. Admission is ten dollars at the door, including a snack and non-alcoholic drink, and free for members.

Other Programming

Keepsake House runs additional literary and community arts programming beyond its monthly Queens open mic series at Grey Studios.

Good to Know

Grey Studios LIC is located at 39-45 Crescent Street in Long Island City.

title: Chano's Cantina
venue_description:
Chano's Cantina

Chano's Cantina is a Mexican restaurant and bar in Astoria that pairs its regular dinner and drinks service with a weekly open mic night.

Atmosphere and Setting

The cantina has a relaxed, family-friendly feel, drawing a mixed neighborhood crowd for food and drinks alongside performers testing out new material.

Open Mic Night

Every Wednesday from 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM, with sign-up starting at 7:30 PM, Chano's runs a family-friendly open mic hosted by Michael Lloret, welcoming musicians and other performers for a relaxed neighborhood evening.

Other Programming

Chano's Cantina functions primarily as a neighborhood restaurant and bar, with the open mic serving as its regular weekly live-entertainment night.

Good to Know

Chano's Cantina is located at 35-55 31st Street in Astoria. It is worth calling ahead to confirm the open mic is running as scheduled.
